newsitem.title: CANADA: Man takes dad's corpse on U.S./Canandian road trip.
newsitem.headline: Man takes dad's corpse on U.S./Canandian road trip.

text.p: Peter Bashucky was still in shock on Wednesday after driving across the United States from California to Canada in four days with his dead father as a macabre travelling companion.
"It was very hard to drive. I had a lot on my mind. It was very hard," Bashucky told Reuters on Wednesday.
He said he was so traumatized when his father died of a massive stroke in Los Angeles last week he could think of nothing but getting the body home to Toronto.
Nicholas Bashucky, 78, a veteran of the Second World War, left seven children and 11 grandchildren.

Peter Bashucky, 46, put his father's body on a bed behind the driver's seat in his recreational vehicle and left Los Angeles on Friday morning. He drove through snow and battering wind, making frequent stops for ice to keep the body cold and sleeping next to it. He reached the Canada-U.S. border at Niagara Falls by midnight on Monday and was waved through.
"When I got to the border I was only asked if I had anything to declare, any alcohol or tobacco. I said I didn't smoke and I only had one bottle," Bashucky said.

Customs officer Justin Alvis said Bashucky should have had a coroner's report saying how his father had died. But he was uncertain if crossing the border with an undeclared corpse constituted a violation of customs law.
Bashucky continued to Toronto, arriving late in the afternoon, and slept for eight hours before contacting his brother and calling a nearby funeral home. A funeral is planned for next Monday.
Nicholas Bashucky will be buried next to his wife, who died in 1987.
